content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts show upward drift (increasing trend) even when true values exhibit sharp declines or mean reversion.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes in history — model reacts too aggressively, peaking too early.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the latter half of the forecast — true values often drop after initial peaks.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting model lacks downward adjustment mechanism.
- Model underreacts to recent low prices — fails to anticipate sharp drops following high peaks.
- Forecasts are too smooth — lack volatility matching observed price swings in true data.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — true values often dip before forecast adjusts.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually flatten — mismatch with true volatility patterns.
- Model does not adjust for seasonality or policy-driven price shocks — overestimates long-term trend.
